title.en: How Would You Welcome an Overnight Guest?
title.zh: 朋友住一晚：你会怎样介绍这个家？

description.en: Six fictional short-stay choices about a simple house note, a shared first tour and asking as needs arise. Find your guest-orientation style.
description.zh: 六次虚构短住选择，留简单居家便条、一起走一小圈、需要时再问，发现你会怎样帮来客熟悉环境。

introduction.en: Imagine a welcome overnight visit that both people have agreed to. The quiz focuses on how you explain an unfamiliar space and its ordinary routines, not how luxurious your home is or how much work a host should do.
introduction.zh: 想象双方已同意的一次受欢迎过夜来访。题目只看怎样介绍陌生空间与普通日常，不评家多豪华，也不规定主人该付出多少劳动。

focus.en: Helping a guest become oriented through a short written guide, a shared walkthrough or a responsive ask-as-needed approach.
focus.zh: 通过短文字说明、共同走看或需要时回应，帮助来客熟悉环境。

prompt.en: Your guest has just arrived. You offer…

label.en: A short note with the few practical things they need.
label.zh: 一张写少数所需实际信息的短便条。

label.en: A brief walk through the shared parts of the home.
label.zh: 一起简短走看家里共用部分。

label.en: An invitation to ask about things as they come up.
label.zh: 遇到需要时再问的邀请。

prompt.en: You have only a little time before your own activity. You…
prompt.zh: 自己的活动前只剩一点时间，你会……

label.en: Show the essential places together and leave the rest for later.
label.zh: 一起看必要位置，其余留稍后。

label.en: Leave a clear small written orientation the guest can revisit.
label.zh: 留清楚小文字说明，方便回看。

label.en: Say when you are available for questions and what they can use meanwhile.
label.zh: 说明何时可问、期间可用什么。

prompt.en: The guest wants to be independent during the stay. You…
prompt.zh: 朋友希望住时自在独立，你会……

label.en: Make a simple guide to the agreed common items.
label.zh: 给已约共用品一份简单指引。

label.en: Ask which one thing they still want explained.
label.zh: 问仍想听解释的哪一件事。

label.en: Offer one short walkthrough, then leave them room to settle.
label.zh: 提供一次短走看，再留安顿空间。

prompt.en: An ordinary house routine differs from theirs. You…
prompt.zh: 一个普通居家习惯与对方不同，你会……

label.en: Explain it when it becomes relevant and ask what arrangement would fit.
label.zh: 相关时再解释，也问怎样安排合适。

label.en: Show the routine once in its actual place.
Add one clear line to the small house note.
label.zh: 给小便条添一行清楚说明。

prompt.en: A repeated small question comes up. You…
prompt.zh: 一个小问题反复出现，你会……

label.en: Put the answer where the guest can easily find it.
label.zh: 把答案放在来客容易找到的地方。

label.en: Offer to show the relevant spot once more without making it a test.
label.zh: 再示范一次相关位置，不把它当考试。

label.en: Ask whether a different explanation would be more useful.
label.zh: 问换种说明是否更有用。

prompt.en: What would make the visit feel well oriented?
prompt.zh: 怎样会让来访者熟悉得舒服？

label.en: We had a shared picture of the space without a long lecture.
label.zh: 不用长讲课，也有一份共同空间图。

label.en: The guest could return to useful information independently.
label.zh: 来客可独立回看有用信息。

label.en: Questions could be asked without embarrassment as needs changed.
label.zh: 需要变化时，也可不尴尬地问。

summary.en: Your welcome leaves a few useful facts where the guest can return to them. A note can give independence without requiring somebody to memorize a tour. The portrait values a practical information format rather than the quality or size of your home.
summary.zh: 你愿意把几条有用信息留成小便条，让客人需要时可以回来查看。不必刚到就记住一整段介绍，也能自己找到需要的东西。这是在描述一种信息提供方式，不是在评价家的大小或好坏。

example.en: You might leave a small card showing where agreed shared cups and spare blankets are, alongside the time you both chose for the next morning.
example.zh: 你可能留张小卡，写清约好可以共用的杯子、备用毯子放在哪，也记下双方商量好的第二天早晨安排。

strength.en: A short reference can reduce repeated guessing and let the guest use ordinary shared space without needing to interrupt every time.
strength.zh: 一份简短说明，可以减少反复猜测。客人使用共用空间时，也不必每次都打断主人询问。

tradeoff.en: A note can become a wall of rules if every preference is included. Keeping only the useful shared details leaves room for an actual visit.
tradeoff.zh: 如果把每个偏好都写进去，便条也会变成满墙规则。只留下真正有用的共用信息，才能给实际相处留空间。

experiment.en: For a willing short stay, write three practical details the guest asked for or will actually use. Leave the rest open to a simple question.
experiment.zh: 有客人短住时，写三条对方问过、或确实用得上的信息。其他事情，让客人需要时简单问一句就好。

summary.en: Your guest’s first orientation happens in the space itself. A short shared walk lets a name connect with an actual place. This result describes an introduction style, not a requirement to guide or entertain a visitor throughout the stay.
summary.zh: 你愿意先和客人走一小圈，把名称和实际位置对上。简短介绍有助于安顿，但不代表你要整个住宿期间一直带领或安排娱乐。

example.en: You might show the agreed common shelf and a comfortable place for the guest’s bag, then let them settle without narrating every object in the room.
example.zh: 你可能指出已约共用架与可放包的位置，就让朋友安顿，不把房间每件东西都讲一遍。

strength.en: Seeing a few places together can make instructions easier to picture and give a guest a concrete reference for a later question.
strength.zh: 一起看看几个位置，说明就更具体，客人之后提问时也有一个知道在哪的参照。

tradeoff.en: A first tour can contain more than a tired guest wants to take in. A brief version and permission to ask again can work better than completeness.
tradeoff.zh: 刚到的客人也许很累，未必想一次记很多东西。介绍短一点，并允许以后再问，可能比讲得面面俱到更合适。

experiment.en: Offer a short orientation to a willing guest and ask which place matters first. Stop after the useful part rather than finishing an imagined full tour.
experiment.zh: 如果客人愿意，先问最想知道哪个位置，再做一个简短介绍。讲完此刻有用的部分就可以停，不必走完预想的全程。

summary.en: Your welcome keeps questions ordinary as the stay unfolds. You do not need to predict every need in advance. The portrait values an available response while leaving both host and guest free to have their own time.
summary.zh: 你希望客人住下来后，有问题时也能自然地问，不必第一天就预料所有需要。愿意回应，同时也让主人和客人各自保留自己的时间。

example.en: You might explain the few essentials first and say when you can answer other questions, so the guest does not need to store a long list of information immediately.
example.zh: 你可能先介绍几件必要的事，再说清其他问题什么时候方便问。客人就不用一到场便记住长长一串信息。

strength.en: A responsive approach can make the explanation fit the question actually being asked and keep a short visit from beginning with too many assumptions.
strength.zh: 需要时再说明，可以让回答贴近真实问题，也避免短住一开始就加入太多没确认的假设。

tradeoff.en: An invitation to ask can feel vague if the host is unavailable without saying so. Naming a simple contact or timing arrangement helps it work.
tradeoff.zh: 如果说“随时问”，却没说明自己什么时候不方便，客人还是难以判断。说清联系办法或方便回应的时间，会更实用。

experiment.en: Tell a willing guest the essentials and one clear way to ask later. Give an honest time boundary rather than promising constant availability.
experiment.zh: 告诉客人几件必要的事，再说明以后有问题可以怎样问。诚实说清方便回应的时间，不必承诺一直在线。

topic.zh: 留宿客人欢迎方式测试

title.zh: 留宿客人欢迎方式测试

description.en: Welcome an imagined overnight guest with a short note, a walkthrough or responsive questions. Six choices explore making a visit easier without guessing every preference.
description.zh: 用简短说明、共同走一遍或随需询问，欢迎想象中的留宿客人。六次选择，让到访好适应，不必猜全所有偏好。

question.en: Is a written guest note a substitute for asking what someone wants?
question.zh: 写好住宿说明，就不必再问客人需要什么吗？

answer.en: A note can explain practical information, a walkthrough makes spaces familiar, and questions handle needs that arise later. They can complement one another; a prepared welcome does not require predicting everything about a guest.
answer.zh: 说明能交代实用信息，走一遍让空间熟悉，询问处理后来出现的需要。三者可互补；准备欢迎不等于预知客人的一切。
